findings.what: ownerHint() picks the first document in the array carrying a non-null acceptedByName and renders "{name} accepted the previous ones" for every non-owner viewing a not-live standing, regardless of which of the two legal kinds is actually the one blocking standing_live. In the legal_standing_new_version scenario the unaffected kind's still-current acceptor would be named as having accepted "the previous ones", which is not quite what happened (their acceptance of the OTHER kind is still current).
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/firm-commercial-settings.test.mjs's p635.db.legal_standing_new_version cell and the migration's own limb-(a) logic (0233:243-256) show standing can go false while one kind's acceptance is still fully valid; legal-standing-card.tsx:178 does `documents.find(d => d.acceptedByName !== null)` with no per-kind targeting. The unit test at legal-standing-card.test.tsx:105-119 only asserts a substring ("An owner of this firm must accept the current versions") that matches both the named and unnamed hint variants, so it would not catch a wrong name being picked.
